verification_report.summary: All three supplied assertions pass sequential verification. For the exact star, the comparison conditions form a decreasingly closed sheaf, the finite-point inequalities yield the stated finite slopes and countable activity, and finite harmonic smoothing with the explicit error margins gives decreasing approximants on one fixed neighbourhood. The polar-node and terminal-endpoint cases are valid. For the Stone–Euclidean product, the countable Boolean algebra gives the required common metrizable quotient; clopen upper envelopes, convolution, and the tail correction establish first-stage approximation, including dimension zero. For the Stone–star product, compactness supplies a common countable activity set under sequential limits, compact parameter suprema preserve endpoint traces and junction inequalities, and finite branch truncation followed by harmonic smoothing preserves decrease. Uniform endpoint approximation follows on a smaller compact terminal interval from the earlier continuous decreasing construction. All cited CLD definitions and applications were checked against the [2025 primary text](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~antoine.chambert-loir/publications/papers/fdceb-20250725.pdf), following theorem-search queries and web fallback. No critical errors or mathematical gaps were found.
